prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1096; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness and states she has not yet seen a physician. No attorney involved at this stage; claimant is handling communications directly.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. She describes onset of neck strain within hours of impact, with pain radiating into the upper shoulder and limited range of motion when turning her head. Advised her of the process for medical documentation and recommended she obtain an evaluation as soon as possible. She confirmed she has an appointment scheduled.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by claimant showing rear bumper damage to the third-party vehicle and minor crush damage to the claimant's rear panel. Police report notes the at-fault driver admitted to looking at a phone before impact. Liability appears clear. Requested the urgent care visit record and any prescribed treatment plan.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the treating clinic. Diagnosis is cervical strain with muscle spasm, treated with rest, a short course of muscle relaxants, and physical therapy referral. Prognosis noted as good with expected recovery within several weeks. No fractures or imaging-confirmed soft tissue injury reported. Claimant has not yet requested a settlement figure.

Entry 5: Followed up with claimant regarding physical therapy progress. She reports pain has decreased and she has returned to most daily activities, though she still experiences stiffness after long periods of driving. Explained the general claim evaluation steps and that a settlement evaluation will be prepared once treatment is complete. Claimant indicated she understands and will call back with questions. File remains open pending final treatment update.
